Sparse lazy seeds

Source: R/lazy-sparse.R
lazy-sparse.Rd

A StoreSparseSeed is a DelayedArray seed for a CSR or CSC Element on disk, in h5ad or zarr (v3 and v2). It wraps a backed_sparse over the store, so it reads indptr once and then only the slices of data and indices that a block needs, and the same code serves every format. Blocks stay sparse: extract_sparse_array() gives an SVT_SparseMatrix (SparseArray) and is_sparse() is TRUE.

Usage

store_sparse_seed(store, path, chunks = NULL, call = rlang::caller_env())

# S4 method for class 'StoreSparseSeed'
dim(x)

# S4 method for class 'StoreSparseSeed'
dimnames(x)

# S4 method for class 'StoreSparseSeed'
extract_sparse_array(x, index)

# S4 method for class 'StoreSparseSeed'
extract_array(x, index)

store_sparse_values(x)

Arguments

store

An open store handle, see io-store.

path

Absolute path of the sparse matrix Element.

chunks

Optional chunk shape, two entries.

call

The call reported by errors.

x

A StoreSparseSeed.

index

A list with one entry per dimension, NULL (every index) or a vector of positions.

Details

As for lazy-dense, type() is fixed from the On-disk dtype of data (logical for bool, integer for int8, int16, int32, uint8 and uint16 and double otherwise), and store_sparse_values() gives the matrix with the On-disk dtype record that read_h5ad() gives.

chunkdim() follows Python's read_elem_lazy() for sparse groups: the major axis (rows for CSR, columns for CSC) is cut every 1000 positions or every chunks entry (NA or -1 for the whole axis), and the minor axis is never cut, so chunks may only be the axis length, -1 or NA there. An axis of length 0 has a chunk of 0, as in Python.
